messages:
maria: Running the quickstart inside a Docker container and my first request is getting 403 Payment Required. I set REDWOOD_API_KEY in the env to the key from the onboarding email.

maria: docker run cmd: `docker run -e REDWOOD_API_KEY=ws_ABC123 sample-app:latest ./start.sh`

maria: logs: ```
[2026-03-20T12:03:10Z] POST /v1/chat -> 403 Payment Required: workspace billing not configured
```

devx-bot: automated message: Your request hit the billing gate for workspace ws_ABC123 — see https://console.redwood.ai/orgs/ws_ABC123/billing to add a card or apply credits.

aiden: that looks like a workspace (ws_) key. Quicknote: workspace keys will 403 if the workspace has no billing method or quota. Service account keys (sa_) bypass that gating for service workloads.

maria: ah, I thought the onboarding key would just work for quickstarts. Is there a way the quickstart can detect this and print a clearer message?

shreya: yeah we should detect ws_ prefix and suggest actions. Meanwhile can you run a curl to sanity-check the key? `curl -s -I -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models`

maria: here's the curl output: ```
HTTP/1.1 403 Payment Required
content-type: application/json

{"error":"workspace_billing_required","message":"Workspace needs billing configured to use generation APIs"}
```

kevin: confirm: if you go to Console -> Billing for that workspace you'll either add a card or apply credit. For quick dev you can create a service key instead via the CLI: `redwood keys create --type=service` (the key starts with sa_).

maria: I don't see Billing in the console UI for that workspace — maybe I wasn't an admin on that specific workspace. How do I check permissions?

shreya: Console -> Members -> your user. If you're not admin ask the org owner to add billing or to create a service key. Alternatively create a new workspace (you'll be owner) and use that for the quickstart.

maria: ok asked the owner, they said they'd add a card. while waiting I created a service key from my personal admin workspace and swapped env to sa_tmp123 then re-ran the container.

maria: success! logs now: ```
[2026-03-20T12:18:21Z] POST /v1/chat -> 200 OK
{"id":"chat_01","choices":[{"text":"Hello from Redwood quickstart!"}]}
```

maria: :tada: firstcall succeeded from inside the container. thanks for the pointers.

kevin: filing a small DX bug to update the quickstart script to validate key prefixes and print a targeted message ("Looks like a workspace key: ensure billing is set or use a service key"). I'll add a note to the onboarding doc.

maria: happy to open the PR with the wording change + a hint about how to create a service key.

devx-bot: created issue #4527: "quickstart: detect workspace (ws_) keys and surface clearer billing guidance" - link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/devex/issues/4527

shreya: tiny follow-up: we should also ensure the Docker sample checks env and exits with a helpful message instead of letting the app continue and fail later.

maria: agreed. also adding a short troubleshooting bullet to the README about admin/owner permissions for billing.

aiden: nice win — glad the service key unblocked you.

maria: thanks everyone!
